title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Marisol Vega
description: Motivation: production workloads showed intermittent tail-latency spikes under mixed priority traffic and long-running generation requests. The continuous batcher scheduler was favoring large, high-throughput streams and starving small/interactive requests; timeouts were occasionally too aggressive and queueing thresholds were not adaptive to throughput patterns. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing behavior, enforce stronger fairness (priority + age-based), add starvation prevention via request aging, and make timeouts/configs more conservative and observable. Summary of changes: updated scheduler to a hybrid priority-age queue (priority first, then age within priority), introduced an adaptive queue-length threshold based on recent throughput and GPU utilization, added per-request "enqueue_age" to allow starvation prevention (requests promoted after an age threshold), tightened windowing for continuous-batcher timeouts and exposed new knobs: max_enqueue_time_ms, default_priority_boost_ms, adaptive_queue_alpha. Added metrics for queued_age_histogram, promoted_requests_count, queue_drops_by_reason and scheduler_decisions_explainer to help debug fairness decisions. Checklist: - [x] Design + perf sims (ENG-3219) - [x] Implementation in scheduler and config defaults - [x] Unit + integration tests for fairness & timeouts - [x] Microbenchmark results and end-to-end regression tests - [x] Docs & runtime flags for rollout Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout (continuous-batcher.scheduler.fairness_v2) with canary on Dedicated pools, 2h ramp and metric alerts on tail latency and promoted_request ratios. If tail latency or queue drops increase by >10% during canary, auto-disable and revert to previous policy. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps defaults conservative (no immediate perf regression expected). The behavioral change is most visible when mixed priority workloads are present or when a few long sequences would otherwise dominate batching resources. See linked Linear items for sims and incident context.
